newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Danubius says to buy Hungaria hotels with loans.
newsitem.headline: Danubius says to buy Hungaria hotels with loans.

text.p: Danubius Hotels will finance its 8.125 billion forint acquisition of the state-owned hotels group Hungaria Szalloda Rt through loans and not by a rights issue, company officials said on Monday.
"We've organised the financing, the money's lined up," Bernard D. Schreier, president of Danubius's UK-based majority shareholder CP Holding, told Reuters.
"We'll have a rights issue eventually but not for the moment," he added.
Danubius President and CEO Sandor Betegh confirmed to Reuters that the sale will be financed through a bridging loan. "It will be a bridging loan but I can't give further details as yet," he said.

Both men were speaking after the ceremony to sign the contract for the sale of Hungaria Szalloda between Danubius and the state privatisation agency APV, under whose ownership Danubius was placed prior to the sell-off.

Schreier said Danubius may use a rights issue to finance modernisation under the terms of the contract, which stipulates that the mew owner must refurbish the 14-hotel chain at a cost of two billion forints over three years.
He added the amount of the equity raise will depend on the financial situation at Hungaria.
"We want to know the cash-flow situation from HungarHotels, which we haven't got so far, and we need to raise the money for the renovation," he said.
Danubius won the privatisation tender for 85 percent of Hungaria by offering 8.125 billion forints for the shares, worth 4.675 billion forints at face value.
The deal is subject to approval by the Competition Office, which can prohibit the transaction if the Danubius and Hungaria account for more than 30 percent of the domestic hotels market.
Analysts said earlier that depending on how this is calculated the two firms' market share is just below that figure.

Since the August announcement of the sale Danibus's share price on the Budapest Stock Exchange has risen steadily from around 2,500 forints to a high on Monday of 3,200. The share ended Monday trade at 3,160.
Betegh said he believed the price could go higher. "I still think it's undervalued," he said.

Hungaria Szalloda Rt operates seven hotels in Budapest and another seven out of the capital. Its predecessor, HungarHotels also owned the Budapest Forum, but this was hived off for a separate sell-off after a failed attempt to privatise the entire group in 1994.

Last month the state privatisation agency APV announced that Intercontinental Hotels had won the tender to buy the Forum. Intercontinental will pay $49.4 million, or 190 percent of face value, for a 94.91 percent stake.
